name: Pulse 64
tagline: Know your machine: every part, live readings and benchmarks, on your phone and PC. Offline, no ads.
overview: Pulse 64 shows what your phone or PC is doing right now: CPU speed for every core, memory, storage, network, battery charge, heat and power draw, around a spinning see-through hologram of your own device. On a folding phone it adds a face panel for the front screen and a charging screen that comes up by itself when you plug in. Run the arcade-style benchmarks, build your own panel, and color the hologram your way. It works offline, with no ads and no accounts, and anything the device doesn't share says so instead of making up a number.

capabilities.title: First run in one tap
capabilities.text: The first time it opens it asks PLAYER 1 to choose a look: Dark, Light or follow the phone.

proofs.caption: First run: PLAYER 1 · CHOOSE YOUR LOOK

capabilities.title: Live dashboard
capabilities.text: Time, uptime, date and device across the top, a SYSTEM STATUS line with a heat light, then power and heat, CPU, every core, memory, storage, network and system cards, all live.

proofs.caption: Live dashboard: plugged-in banner, top bar, status line, power and heat, CPU, cores
Further down: network and system cards, then Benchmarks, Panel Studio, face panel and charging screen

capabilities.title: The hologram stays pinned
capabilities.text: A spinning see-through picture of your phone stays at the top while the readings scroll up under it.

proofs.caption: Scrolled down: the hologram stays put, the cards slide under it

capabilities.title: Spinning see-through hologram
capabilities.text: Your phone drawn in glowing red light, inside and out: board, chips, battery and charging coil. It spins on its own and you can drag it to spin it.

proofs.caption: Dragging the hologram to spin it (from the demo clip)

capabilities.title: Follows the screen's shape
capabilities.text: A folded front screen gets a tall layout, an opened Fold gets a menu on the left, and a wide screen gets its own layout. It switches by itself.

proofs.caption: Folded front screen (1080×2520): tall layout
Opened-Fold layout with the NAVIGATING menu on the left

capabilities.title: Open panel on wide screens
capabilities.text: On a wide screen the readings spread out with no boxes: memory, CPU and battery big across the top, power, heat, storage and network below, the device spinning at the bottom.

proofs.caption: Wide screen (2520×1080): the open panel

capabilities.title: Core view
capabilities.text: The hologram fills the screen behind, with eight see-through tiles around it: CPU speed and heat, memory, storage, battery, charging, download and upload.

proofs.caption: Settings → Dashboard layout → Core view

capabilities.title: Up Close
capabilities.text: Tap the hologram to open it full screen. Drag to turn it any way, switch between Phone, Folded and Open, and reset the view.

proofs.caption: Tap the hologram: Up Close, Phone shape
Open: a book fold laid flat, hinge modules down the middle
Drag to turn it

capabilities.title: How far open
capabilities.text: A slider opens the folding picture from shut to flat, and the hinge readout follows.

proofs.caption: How far open set to 90°: HINGE 90° under the name

capabilities.title: Follows your real hinge
capabilities.text: On a phone with a hinge sensor the picture opens and closes with the phone.

capabilities.title: Hologram colors
capabilities.text: Six parts of the hologram, each with its own color, strength and light/dark sliders, plus ready-made looks. The picture changes live.

proofs.caption: Hologram colors: Pulse red
Ready-made look: Ice blue
Ready-made look: Silver + red
Body color slider moved: the frame turns green

capabilities.title: Knows your phone's shape
capabilities.text: The hologram is drawn in your phone's real proportions, camera layout and buttons from a built-in list of 114 phones and tablets.

capabilities.title: Benchmarks
capabilities.text: PRESS START runs five tests in about 12 seconds: CPU one core, CPU all cores, memory speed, storage write and storage read. Each bar compares this run with your best.

proofs.caption: Running: STAGE 2 OF 5 · ALL 4 CORES
Done: STAGE CLEAR · SCORE, and NEW HIGH SCORE!

capabilities.title: HIGH SCORES table
capabilities.text: A new best asks for your three initials and goes on an arcade HIGH SCORES table, top ten.

proofs.caption: Entering initials (demo initials PLS)
HIGH SCORES: 1ST PLS with the date

capabilities.title: GAME OVER: TOO HOT
capabilities.text: If the phone says it's getting too hot, the run stops by itself.

capabilities.title: Panel Studio
capabilities.text: Build your own panel: add readings, hold the yellow MOVE word to drag one, tap it for RESIZE to make it full width, take one off with the red arrow. The preview is live.

proofs.caption: Panel Studio: live preview and your readings
Tap MOVE on Memory used: it turns into RESIZE
Drag right: Memory used is full width
Hold MOVE and drag: Heat moved to the top

capabilities.title: Panel size, columns and color
capabilities.text: Tile size, 1–3 columns and Red / Amber / Cyan / Green change the whole panel. Show it on the face panel and the charging screen.

proofs.caption: Small tiles, 3 columns, Cyan, two readings added
Show my panel on the face panel and the charging screen: On

capabilities.title: Panel file
capabilities.text: Save your panel as a file to back it up or share it, and load one back, through the phone's own file picker. No storage permission.

proofs.caption: Save the panel to a file: Panel saved to the file
Load a panel file: the phone's own picker shows the saved panel
Loaded back: the same size, columns and color

capabilities.title: Face panel
capabilities.text: A big clock, the date, the charge line, the spinning hologram and your own panel on black, made for the folded front screen.

proofs.caption: Face panel on the folded front screen, with my cyan panel

capabilities.title: Face panel on the lock screen
capabilities.text: Turn it on and the face panel is waiting on the lock screen every time the screen goes off. Unlock and it steps aside.

capabilities.title: Charging screen
capabilities.text: Pick it once as Android's screen saver and it comes up by itself every time the phone charges.

proofs.caption: Android screen saver: Pulse 64 charging screen picked
Preview: the charging screen, tall
The charging screen on a wide screen

capabilities.title: Live wallpaper
capabilities.text: The spinning hologram of your phone behind your home-screen icons, with the time, date and charge on it if you want.

proofs.caption: Set the hologram as my wallpaper: Android's preview
Spinning, with the info panel tucked away

capabilities.title: Settings
capabilities.text: Look, text size, °F/°C, update speed, face panel, layout, red sweep, hologram size and colors, clock look, wallpaper options, support and crash log.

proofs.caption: Settings, top
Settings: red sweep, panel look, hologram, clock, wallpaper
Settings: wallpaper options, support and crash log, About

capabilities.title: °F or °C
capabilities.text: One tap changes every temperature.

proofs.caption: Settings → Temperature → °C
The dashboard now says 25.0 °C (it said 77.0 °F)

capabilities.title: Light and dark at a tap
capabilities.text: The half-circle button flips the whole app between dark and light, from any screen.

proofs.caption: Tap the half-circle: the light look

capabilities.title: Manual on every screen
capabilities.text: The ghost “i” opens a plain-words manual: what each part is and how to set it up.

proofs.caption: The manual

capabilities.title: Crash log and Report a problem
capabilities.text: Settings keeps a crash log you can read, and Report a problem opens your own email with the details.

proofs.caption: Show the crash log: No crashes recorded.

capabilities.title: Never a made-up number
capabilities.text: Anything the device doesn't share says N/A or “not shared”, never a guess.

proofs.caption: GPU LOAD: N/A, not shared by this phone (top middle)
PC: CPU temperature and fans say N/A until Deep Sensors (bottom)

capabilities.title: Offline, no ads
capabilities.text: No internet permission. Nothing you see leaves the phone. No ads, no accounts.

proofs.caption: Settings → About: No internet permission

capabilities.title: Back goes back to the Pulse app that opened it
capabilities.text: Opened from another Pulse app, Back returns you there instead of to the home screen.

capabilities.title: Windows: live readings
capabilities.text: On the PC: CPU load overall and per thread, memory, disk, network, and NVIDIA graphics temperature, load, clock and power, in the same bars as the phone.

proofs.caption: PC live page, dark. Drawn by the app's own drawing code in the farm build check, with test readings; not a desktop screenshot
PC live page, light, narrow window (same build check)

capabilities.title: Windows: parts list
capabilities.text: This PC: processor, motherboard, BIOS, every memory stick, graphics, drives, network adapters and Windows version.

capabilities.title: Windows: tray and settings
capabilities.text: Closing the window rests it in the tray, where it reads nothing. Settings: look, text size, °F/°C, update speed, start with Windows, Report a problem.

demo.caption: 30 seconds on the test bench: the live dashboard, dragging the hologram, scrolling the cards under it, then Up Close: open the fold, set it to 90° and turn it.

note: Phone pictures: Android v0.13.5 on our test bench (an Android emulator with a Fold-size screen), not a real phone, so the device shown is a generic test phone. PC pictures: Windows v0.1.1 from the farm's drawing check, with test readings.
